title: Fourier regularity and restriction means
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube. Its Fourier coefficients vanish on every nonempty set of at most $k$ coordinates if and only if, for every coordinate set $J$ and every assignment of signs to the coordinates outside $J$ such that the complement of $J$ has cardinality at most $k$, the mean of the resulting restriction of $f$ to the coordinates in $J$ equals the mean of $f$ on the full cube.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
An arbitrary fixed sign assignment on the complement of $J$
The complement of $J$ has cardinality at most $k
